description: Facebook 584 — 101 patches with Vietnamese UI, Following feed by default, save photos by default + hide tab bar on the Reels tab (on by default; hiding gives the bar's space back, a tap or swipe brings it back for three seconds; 0.17.8: giving the space back is re-asserted on every layout pass from the bar's own tree — the live pager is found from the bar and its bottom padding, and its pages', is taken again whenever Facebook settles it back — and the Reels page's own header hides too, on its own switch in Appearance, its height collapsed so reels get that space, back for three seconds on a touch) + experimental: push the video to the top when comments open (settings > Comments) + split the screen half and half when comments open, EXTENDED in 0.17.8 (the Hook diagnostics row proved the in-place controller path is never reached on the test phone — zero calls while real comments opened — so the half cap now also stands on the surfaces that phone can take: the regular comment sheet, its share capped where its parameters are built and its window height capped at both places the popover fragment settles it, the fixed eight-tenths box a full share falls back to included; and the video platform's split screen, its sheet height capped where it is handed to the sheet's component. The five split-screen launchers and the comment views setup only report that they ran, so the Hook diagnostics row — itself extended with the hunt's last-seen shares, ratio and heights — can say which surface a phone really opens comments through; on by default, settings > Comments). FITTED in 0.17.9: capping the sheet still left the video full-screen behind it, its lower half hidden under the sheet, so while a comment sheet is open the playing video's container is now settled into exactly the space the sheet leaves — the page's width, from the page's top down to the sheet's top edge — and the player re-fits the whole frame inside it, centred, as large as its aspect allows; closing the sheet gives the container back + tab bar background more transparent, about half of Facebook's own alpha (on by default, settings > Appearance; 0.17.9: on the Reels tab the bar's fills are fully transparent and the opaque backgrounds of the pager, the Reels page and the bar's frame are cleared, while the reel's video container is lengthened to the bottom of the screen, so a reel runs to the bottom edge under the bar) + the Hook diagnostics row (settings > Pause, backup and diagnostics); quiet preset. FIXED in 0.17.10: the Hook diagnostics row on 0.17.9 proved both 0.17.9 mechanisms never once fired on the test phone, for landscape and portrait videos alike — the video fit's hunt never recorded a container, and the bottom clearing stood at 'not applied yet'. The hunt is rewritten: any video surface at least half the window's width and a twelfth of its height is a candidate now (the first shape demanded near half the window's height, which a 16:9 player — a strip a quarter of the window tall — can never meet), scored by the part of it on screen, walked as deep as the activity's content tree asks from the comment fragment's own activity (so Reels, Watch and feed players are all covered), and retried on the sheet window's own draws for about two seconds instead of three fixed delays; when it still does not land, the diagnostics row says how many tries it made, the largest surface it met and why it stopped. The bottom clearing now leaves its reason as its state at every way out (not the Reels tab, the switch off, no pager found), takes any kind of background rather than only a plain colour, adds the tab bar's ancestors on the way to the window, and the video's distance to the bottom of its page and of the window is measured on every Reels pass in either state of the bar, so the band's own numbers are always on the row. FIXED in 0.17.11: the 0.17.10 measured fit was real and invisible - the diagnostics row read the video container taken from 2107px to exactly the region's 1187px, fitted and restored once each, and the phone's screen never moved: Facebook's layout took the params back within a pass or two, and the hold stood on the sheet window's tree, not the activity's where the container lives. The comments fit no longer touches the layout at all: the found container keeps Facebook's own layout and is drawn into the region above the comment sheet by a uniform scale about its top centre (factor = the region's height over the container's own height), translated so its top rests on the region's top and its centre on the region's centre - the player renders the whole frame into its surface and the surface is drawn at the scale, so the whole frame stands inside the region with nothing cropped and no layout pass able to settle it back. A guard on the activity decor's layout passes watches the drawn box while the sheet is open and scales afresh from a clean identity measurement when the box is out of place, re-hunting (throttled) if the page rebuilt the container; closing the sheet restores the found transform exactly. Diagnostics keeps the scale factor and the drawn top/bottom against the region's, sticky. The Reels bottom numbers are sticky too: the clear keeps its last conclusion reached on the Reels tab (with its cleared count) instead of being overwritten by whatever tab the row is read from, the locate walk runs on the hunt's full 60000-node budget and caches the container between passes so the bottom gaps are measured as designed, and the bottom work climbs past the page - the first box from the page upward whose bottom stops short of the window's bottom is lengthened to the window's bottom (bottom margin given back first, an exact height grown by the rest; a box whose params hold nothing hands the climb to its parent and the passes converge level by level), its class name and total lengthened px kept on the diagnostics row, its found params restored on leaving the tab. Scope: layout-made black only - a 16:9 frame's own letterbox on a portrait page is aspect, not layout, and is not cropped away. FITTED TO THE FRAME in 0.17.13: the scale fitted the container, a portrait box whose landscape frame is only a strip letterboxed in its middle, so a 16:9 video came out at about a third of the area it could have had, floating mid-region. The fit now measures the picture itself - the frame as the player draws it, its surface sized to the frame and centred in its box by the player's own resize - and scales by the picture's fit into the region, the smaller of the region's shares of its width and of its height, set at the region's top and centred across it: a 16:9 frame in the phone's region takes no scale at all and lands whole at its full width, a portrait frame is fitted by the region's height. The guard above the sheet watches the picture's drawn box now, and the diagnostics row gains the picture's own line - its size and place before the fit, the box it was fitted to, and the shape it was read from. + NEW in 0.17.12: 'Swipe up or down on the mini player to switch videos' - a hard fling up on the small floating player a video shrinks into plays the next video in its chain and a hard fling down goes back to the one before, through the chain's own stock advance; the extension keeps the session's history itself, so going forward again replays what was stepped back over before new videos are taken from the chain. Dragging the player, tapping it and weaker flings stay stock. On by default; switch in Hushfacebook settings > Playback. The Hook diagnostics page gains the family's block, including whether the server gave the player a chaining session at all and the chain queue's size at the last sighting. + CHANGED in 0.17.14: the mini player swipe answers an ordinary swipe — the fling gate drops from the gesture listener's dismiss threshold (the device's minimum fling velocity scaled by fourteen) to its lower fling threshold (scaled by four), and a firm vertical drag released past half the player's height turns the same page, with the player's drag frozen from the moment the gesture locks vertical, on the enlarged player as on the small one. The Hook diagnostics block keeps the largest fling speed that ever reached the hook and the threshold it was judged against, and counts a switch by fling, a switch by drag and a strong vertical gesture that met neither bar separately. + DISCOVERY in 0.17.15: the Hook diagnostics row on 0.17.14 read the mini player swipe family's hooks called zero times on the test phone while the neighbouring families lived — the chained WatchAndGo player those hooks stand on never opens there. This build carries more than one mini player under one window manager, and which one a phone gets is the launch's choice: the chained player is built only for the launches that carry a chaining session with them, and the rest are handed one of the other managers the app's own wiring provides — a Litho mini player whose view's own touch listener answers nothing, so its taps and drags are settled inside its Litho tree, or the gaming player that floats an instant game. The swipe patch now also stands at the one door every mini player of the family walks through — the window manager's attach, counted under the name of the manager it serves — and counts the gestures that reach the other players' touch listeners, and the family's diagnostics block names the manager that last opened a window, sticky, so one screenshot of the row says which surface the phone really uses and where its touches land. The probe changes nothing it touches, and the swipe itself is unchanged. + NEW in 0.17.16: comments opened from an ordinary post (photo or text) now take 80 percent of the screen — post comments and video comments share one sheet surface in this build, so the share is chosen by what the comments were opened from: a post gets 80 percent, while a video keeps the half-and-half split with the fitted frame above it. The comment sheet's window is also told to resize for the keyboard for the first time (this surface never set it), so tapping the comment box lifts the sheet and the input stays right above the keyboard instead of being covered by it, with the comment list still scrollable above; the Hook diagnostics row records which share was applied and each keyboard lift with the keyboard's height. + FIXED in 0.17.17: three things the 0.17.16 build got wrong on the test phone. The 80 percent post sheet leaked onto reels: a reel's sheet answered 'post' to both of the setup's tests (a reel is not a watch surface and its comment header holds no video), so reel comments lost their half-and-half split. A sheet is now told apart by the split screen family's own test - a playing video surface hunted in the sheet's activity on the fit's own criteria: a video answer at setup settles it at once, and a post answer is only confirmed once the hunt has had a short grace at the sheet's open to find no surface, so the raise lands only on a post for certain; each decision is counted under its own name (raised to 80 percent / kept at half over a video / never settled), and a sheet settled as a post's stands the video fit's own hunt down. The keyboard no longer covers the comment box: the resize flag the last build set changes nothing on this window, so the push is done by hand from the same insets the diagnostics counted - when the keyboard arrives, the sheet's window is stood on the space above it, its bottom lifted by the keyboard's measured height and its height the settled height or what fits above the keyboard, and given back exactly when the keyboard goes; pushes actually applied are counted apart from keyboards merely seen, and the video fit is told the keyboard's height so a fitted frame's region ends at the pushed-up sheet's top. The Reels height chain no longer stops at zero: the box it found held its height as its parent's answer (match parent, no margin), which the old lengthening could not grow. A box with no height of its own is now given an exact one - the height it already measures at, grown by the gap the pass measured - the climb walks the whole chain in the one pass instead of converging level by level, and an ancestor that may clip a directly-set box is asked in the same pass; the diagnostics row records the gap before and after the lengthening and, when a chain still cannot close, the level that blocked it and why. The split family's row also stops reporting two missing anchors for sheets opened over posts: a hunt that finds no video over a photo or text post is what the opening was, not a lost anchor. 0.17.18 adds next and previous buttons inside the system picture-in-picture window: the window's action row is built by one factory for every video surface, and two actions of the fork's own - next video, previous video - are appended after Facebook's skip back, play/pause and skip forward, in their order; a tap turns the playing surface's own pager one page, the turn a swipe makes, and the Hook diagnostics row counts each tap's verdict by name (the host activity last seen, the row's length before and after, the receiver's standing). If Android caps how many actions the window shows, Facebook's own keep their places - the added pair is what the cap leaves out, and the row still reads five in the diagnostics. The same build settles the comment sheet's keyboard push: a keyboard height is applied only once it has settled (read again, or unchanged for about 200ms), a standing push moves only on a real step over 24px, and a settled zero must be repeated and aged before the sheet is given back - the 0.17.17 push chased every mid-slide delivery, flickered for the whole slide and counted 269 pushes with a mid-slide 202px left standing. Push counts are now of settled pushes, and the video fit is fed the settled heights only. 0.17.19 rebuilds the picture-in-picture window's action row to the three actions Android actually draws, on the phone owner's choice — keep the switch buttons, give up the seeks. The factory's list is no longer appended to: the row handed to the window is composed as [previous video, Facebook's own play or pause, next video], and the middle element is the factory's very RemoteAction object lifted out of its list untouched, so its broadcast and the params refresh Facebook runs off the back of it stay stock in every part. The two seek actions leave the window's row while the switch is on — the full player keeps them — and switching it off hands the factory's list through whole again. The hook still stands at the same factory returns, so the refresh that follows any action rebuilds the params through the same composition and the three-button row holds after every tap. The play or pause element is told by the factory's shape, not by its broadcast — no public API hands the Intent back out of a PendingIntent: three actions, play or pause the middle one; one action, the play/pause-only list of a session whose video state is not ready. A list of any other shape, or holding anything that is not a RemoteAction, is not rebuilt on a guess — the pair is appended as 0.17.18 appended, and the shape is counted with its length. The family's diagnostics block names the row the last build composed and counts rebuilds apart from appended shapes. 0.17.20 takes the Reels bottom lengthening to each page as it takes the screen. On the test phone the diagnostics row's Reels bottom lines read "not recorded" through three builds (0.17.16 to 0.17.18) while the first video of a Reels session filled the screen and every video after it stood the same black band short at the bottom for its whole length. Two shapes starved the old pass together: it stood on the tab bar container's own layout, which fires around tab entry and touch holds and never when a reel page turns, so no pass ever visited the pages after the first; and the locate both its measure and its lengthening shared walked the whole window from its decor on a fixed node budget with no geometry pruning, descending every visible subtree — the other tab pages the tab pager keeps alive beside Reels, the reel pager's own off-screen pages — so the budget spent itself in the sibling trees before the player was reached, and both callers then returned writing nothing: no field, no count, no note. The lengthening now rides a watcher on the window's draws, seeded by the hooks that already touch a reel's window — the tab bar's layout on the main screen, a comment sheet's start in any activity, the PiP actions factory's host — so the full-screen viewer a feed or a search opens is served by the same doorbells as the Reels tab. Its walk prunes any subtree lying wholly outside the window before descending, finds the showing page, and serves each page as it takes the screen: the page told by the paging container it sits in, a recycler view included, or as the window's own child for a full-screen page of its own, its container lengthened to the page's bottom and the chain past the page to the window's by the same hands as before, the page before's lengthening given back first so the ancestors the pages share are never lengthened twice, and a standing page re-served only when its gap comes back. Every pass is counted and kept sticky — a page already full height, a pass that finds no page, a chain nothing could lengthen each leave their words — and the tab bar block gains the serve's own lines: the last page and its pager index, its gap before and after, what the serve concluded, and what the walk met, nodes visited and subtrees pruned included. The height chain's note now also answers when the chain already reaches the window's bottom, a conclusion it used to leave blank. No new patch: the bundle still carries 101 patches, all others unchanged. 0.17.21 wires the PiP switch buttons to the surface's real pager: on the test phone the 0.17.19 buttons showed and heard every tap (next x18, previous x6) but all 24 switches were refused with "no video pager in the window" — the tap went looking through the host activity's window while the activity stood in picture-in-picture, and an unpruned walk of that tree spends itself in the sibling trees before it ever reaches the pager, the same wall the reel page serve's pruned walk (0.17.20) exists for; the pager's own scroll methods are renamed in this build besides, so the old reflective names could not have turned a found pager either. The static map this round adds: the pagers of these surfaces are recyclers — the build's SnapRecyclerView (LX/etU;) or a plain RecyclerView under a linear layout manager (FbShortsReelsTabLayoutManager on the Reels tab) — whose pages are their direct children; no controller above the pager offers an advance of its own, and the playing video's state manager still knows no neighbour, so the surface's programmatic turns all land on the pager's own smooth scroll, whose renamed form in this build is told by its body (it hands the turn to the layout manager's smoothScrollToPosition, a name the layout manager kept), as is the renamed adapter-position read (it reads the position out of the child's view holder). The buttons now capture instead of search: every build of the factory's list — which runs as a surface arms, while it stands alive at full size — locates the reel page then showing by the page serve's own candidate rules (the largest video surface, its container, the climb to the paging parent, the full-screen page test) and keeps that page's pager weakly, refreshed at every build. A tap speaks only to the captured pager: it reads the showing page's adapter position off the pager's children, asks the pager for the page one over through its own smooth scroll, and judges the turn after the settle by the position read again — moved is a switch, unmoved a refusal. Every refusal keeps its own counted name (no host, not in PiP, no pager captured, the captured pager gone, the page unreadable, already at the first video, the pager not taking the turn, the pager unmoved), and the family's diagnostics block gains the captured pager's class and the page last read off it, so one screenshot tells which link of the chain a failed switch broke at. The three-button row of 0.17.19, the stock play/pause it reuses, and every other patch are unchanged: the bundle still carries 101 patches.0.17.22: Sửa nút chuyển video PiP không hoạt động: pager của Reel là ViewPager của chính Facebook (lớp đổi tên X.3xR) chứ không phải RecyclerView, nên phép đọc trang cũ chết tại mọi lần chạm (17/17 bị từ chối trên 0.17.21). Nay trang hiện tại được giữ bằng listener sự kiện chọn trang của chính pager ngay từ lúc bắt giữ, lệnh chuyển đi từ chỉ số đã biết bằng method đặt trang của pager và được xác minh qua sự kiện trang mới; chặn nút "kế" ở video cuối theo số trang của adapter. Bắt giữ pager đếm đủ số lần thử/đậu kèm lý do trượt và tự thử lại khi trang chưa dàn xong. Chẩn đoán ghi loại pager, nguồn biết trang và thống kê bắt giữ. FIXED in 0.17.23: the comment keyboard push flickered again in long sessions (0.17.18 was clean in short ones; on the phone a long session read 154 inset deliveries, 111 pushes and the height stuck at a phantom 202px). The cause was self-reference: the insets watcher stood on the comment sheet's own window and read that window's IME inset, while the push rewrites that same window's frame — its y and its height — and the IME inset a window is handed is a function of its own frame, so every push manufactured the next measurement; a phantom that stands still is exactly what the old settle gate believed, and each re-apply minted a fresh phantom for the sheet to chase. The principle is changed, not the thresholds: a height is only ever believed read off the sheet's activity window — a fixed frame the push never touches (the activity decor's root insets); the sheet window's own deliveries now only say that something changed. And an opening LATCHES: one keyboard opening applies AT MOST ONE push. The opening's deliveries only gather candidates; the tallest is applied once, after the height has stood unchanged for ~280ms past the slide's end (mid-slide plateaus like 202px are never believed, since the value rises past them), and from that moment every further delivery of the same opening is ignored — counted as ignored — until the keyboard has closed outright (the raw height at zero and holding zero for 250ms), which alone releases the latch. A panel switch mid-opening (an emoji panel's height) is ignored with the rest: the sheet keeps the place it latched at — steadiness over fine accuracy. The video fit is told the latched height once per opening, and zero at the release. Diagnostics gain a latch row (the opening the session is on, the deliveries the latch has turned away): a clean session reads openings equal to pushes at the keyboard's true ~677px. Test patch run on Facebook 584.0.0.51.56: 101 patches applied, 0 failed.
